# Notation and Conventions

## Basic Sets

- $\mathbb{N}$ denotes the set of natural numbers.
- $\mathrm{WFF}$ denotes the set of well-formed formulas.



## Propositional Variables

We assume a countable family of propositional variables given by

$$
P : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{WFF}, \quad i \mapsto P_i.
$$



## Metavariables

We use the following metavariables:

- $\varphi, \psi, \chi$ for formulas
- $i, j, k \in \mathbb{N}$ for indices



## Logical Connectives

We use the following symbols:

- Negation: $\neg \varphi$
- Conjunction: $\varphi \land \psi$
- Disjunction: $\varphi \lor \psi$



## Parentheses Convention

We omit outer parentheses when there is no ambiguity.



## Inductive Definitions

When defining syntax, we use inductive (recursive) definitions of the form

$$
\varphi ::= \cdots
$$

to describe the formation of well-formed formulas.



## Remarks on Style

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
- $\mathrm{WFF}$ is typeset using $\mathrm{...}$ to distinguish it from variables.
- Logical symbols $\land, \lor, \neg$ are used instead of textual operators.
- We follow a type-theoretic perspective where constructors generate formulas.
:::
